o1.biggest_strength: The numbers are traced and checked (10,900 installs from 76 posts, a projected 6,580 installs against a 3,390 baseline), and the success targets include a mid-point check.
o1.biggest_mistake: The weeks 2 to 4 content is only a one-line angle per week, and the review logic is muddled: it sends all of weeks 2 to 4 for review, yet week 2's Monday 23 Nov post can't go live until the 24th. It also puts a 14:30 afternoon test slot in every week.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep every post in the evening, list the weeks 2 to 4 posts one by one, and say clearly which posts need review and when to submit them.

o2.biggest_strength: It puts everything in the evening and makes narrator clips the core format (4 a week, 16 in the month). It also lists a working title for every post in weeks 2 to 4, and its drafts use the customer's own phrases and the brand line 'Take a breath. You've got this.'
o2.biggest_mistake: The success target is weak: beating the 143-installs-per-post average (about 3,440 in total) is barely above the 90-day baseline, even though the sleep-led mix should do much better. The editor notes also lean on 'pick a clip that mentions X'.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Set a higher install target based on a projection, and write the narrator clip scripts or exact clip picks so the editor has no choices left.

reason: Output 2 sticks to the evening slots, covers all four weeks with a title per post, has a clean no-review week 1 with a fallback, and its drafts sound more like Headspace and its customers. Output 1 has the better install projection and targets, but its afternoon test slot and muddled review timing for weeks 2 to 4 cost it.
